beats.say: Hello! Today we talk about criminals taking over your phone number and stealing your SMS codes.
When a criminal tricks the operator into moving your number to their SIM, your phone suddenly loses signal.

body.text: Emergency calls only. SIM card not recognised.

beats.say: Every year millions of manat are stolen from cards, mostly through shared codes and details.
If your number dies at night, do not wait for morning. Call your operator from another phone.

scenes.title: One in the morning
scenes.intro: It is night and your phone is next to you. Look at each notification and choose the right step.

body.text: Emergency calls only. SIM card not recognised.

actions.label: Call the operator from another phone
actions.feedback: Correct. If your number moved to another card, the operator can block it and give it back to you.

actions.label: Turn the phone off and sleep
actions.feedback: That is exactly what the criminal hopes for. All night your SMS codes will go to them.

steps.label: 00:27 UlduzBank Mobil

body.text: Android, Ganja, 00:27. If this was not you, freeze your card.

steps.say: The SIM is dead, but the bank app still reaches you over home internet.

actions.label: Open the app and freeze the card
actions.feedback: Correct. No money leaves a frozen card, and you can unfreeze it later with the bank.

actions.label: Call the number on the back of the card from another phone
actions.feedback: Right. The number on the card is the real bank, ask them to block the card.

actions.label: Dismiss
actions.feedback: The criminal already receives your SMS codes. They can move money out of the account within minutes.

body.text: Ganja, 00:33. Is this you signing in?

actions.label: Deny
actions.feedback: Well done. The criminal has your number, but this approval exists only on your phone.

actions.label: Approve
actions.feedback: You opened the door yourself. Never approve a request you did not expect, least of all at night.

steps.label: 00:41 Söhbət

title.text: Your account was opened on another phone

body.text: This number was registered on a new device.

steps.say: Your messaging account is tied to your number too.

actions.label: Warn family and friends another way
actions.feedback: Correct. The criminal may ask your family for money in your name, so warn them first.

actions.label: Ignore it
actions.feedback: Tonight your friends may get an urgent money request from you. Warn them now.

steps.label: 08:05 UlduzBank

messages.text: Your card was blocked after suspicious activity. To restore it, enter your card details:

steps.say: In the morning your number is back. Look at this message.

actions.label: Report as spam
actions.feedback: Correct. Criminals use a real incident to strike a second time.

actions.label: Delete
actions.feedback: Right. Sort out card matters only in the bank app or through the number on the card.

actions.label: Open the link
actions.feedback: This is not the bank's site. If you enter your card details, you lose money a second time.

scenes.prompt: Your number suddenly went dead. Put the steps in order.

items.label: Call the operator from another phone and get your number back
Call the bank on the number on your card and freeze the card
Change passwords on key accounts and switch from SMS to an authenticator app
Tell technical support about your work accounts
If money is gone, report it to the police on 102

scenes.explain: First get the number back so new codes stop going to the criminal. Right after that, have the bank freeze your card.

scenes.prompt: Which message is normal and which is a threat? Swipe.

messages.text: Your sign-in code: 482193. Do not tell this code to anyone.

cards.explain: If you asked for this code yourself, it is a normal message. Type the code in yourself and nowhere else.

messages.text: A request to replace the SIM card for your number has been received.

cards.explain: If you did not ask for a new SIM, this is the first sign of an attack. Call your operator at once.

messages.text: Your card is blocked. To unblock it, tell the code you receive to our staff member who calls you.

cards.explain: A bank never asks you to tell a code to its staff. This message is there to steal the code.
Someone signed in from another device while you slept. Freeze the card and call the bank.

body.text: Baku, 09:01. Is this you signing in?

cards.explain: If you are signing in right now, the request is normal. Deny any request you did not expect.

question.prompt: Which protection still works if your number moves to someone else?

options.label: A code sent by SMS
options.feedback: When the number moves to a criminal, the SMS codes go with it. For key accounts this is weak protection.

options.label: An authenticator app or a passkey
options.feedback: Correct. They are tied to your device, not to your SIM card.

options.label: A longer password
options.feedback: A long password is good, but if it can be reset with an SMS code, the criminal still gets in.

scenes.explain: On key accounts like bank, mail and government services, choose an authenticator app or a passkey instead of SMS where you can.

points: If your number suddenly dies, call the operator from another phone at once
Then call the bank and freeze your card
On key accounts use an authenticator app or a passkey instead of SMS
